title: The computer is not connected to the internet
what: It is not connected to any network at the moment.
why: Without a connection you cannot browse, update or sign in to online services.
fix_summary: Open the network helper. It switches on Wi-Fi, restarts the network service and checks the connection.
backup_first: Nothing is changed until you choose.
undo: The helper explains how to undo each step.
manual: Click the network icon, pick your Wi-Fi and enter the password. Or plug in a cable.

title: The network service is not running
what: The part of the system that manages Wi-Fi and cables has stopped, so nothing can connect.
why: It may have crashed or been switched off by mistake.
fix_summary: Start the network service again. Your saved networks are kept.

title: Wi-Fi or Bluetooth is switched off in software
what: Airplane mode or a software switch has turned the radios off.
why: While the radios are off, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth cannot work.
undo: Press the airplane-mode key or run: rfkill block all
manual: Press the airplane-mode key (often Fn plus a key with an aeroplane), or run: rfkill unblock all

title: Wi-Fi is switched off by a physical switch
what: A switch or key on the computer has turned the radios off, and software cannot undo that.
why: Wi-Fi will not work until the switch is turned on.
fix_summary: Nothing can be changed by software.
manual: Look for a slide switch on the side of the laptop, or press the Wi-Fi key (Fn plus a key).

title: A Wi-Fi chip is there but has no driver
why: Without a driver the Wi-Fi chip cannot be used.
fix_summary: Install the missing drivers. Plug in a cable or phone (USB tethering), because this needs the internet.
undo: Remove the package with your package manager if needed.
manual: Connect a cable or tether a phone by USB, then run: sudo secure-linux-drivers install

title: The Wi-Fi chip is missing its firmware file
why: Wi-Fi and some other chips need a small firmware file to work.
fix_summary: Reinstall the hardware firmware package. Needs the internet (use a cable or phone tethering).
undo: Not needed: it only puts files back.
manual: Plug in a cable or tether a phone by USB, then reinstall the linux-firmware package.

title: The Wi-Fi country is not set
what: The Wi-Fi radio does not know which country it is in, so it uses cautious settings. Some networks may be slow or missing.
why: Each country allows different Wi-Fi channels and power, and the 5 GHz band may be limited.
fix_summary: Set the Wi-Fi country so all channels work. It is saved for every start.
backup_first: A copy of the current setting.
manual: Run: sudo iw reg set AU  (use your country code).
notes: asks the country only when it cannot be worked out

title: Connected, but website names do not work
what: The internet connection works, but turning a website name into an address fails, so pages will not open.
why: The name-lookup service (DNS) is stuck or being given bad settings.
fix_summary: Clear the name-lookup memory and restart that service. Your settings are kept.
undo: Not needed: it only resets temporary data.
manual: Run: resolvectl flush-caches, and restart systemd-resolved.

title: This network needs a sign-in page
what: The network asks you to sign in or accept terms in a web page before it allows internet.
why: Hotels, cafes and airports do this. Nothing is wrong with the computer.
manual: Open a web browser and go to http://neverssl.com to get the sign-in page.

title: Connected to the router, but no internet
what: The computer is connected to the network, but the internet cannot be reached.
why: The router may have lost its internet, or the provider may have a fault.
manual: Restart the router (off for 30 seconds). Try another device on the same network.

title: Some websites load slowly or never finish
what: Large pieces of data do not get through this connection, while small ones do. Some pages stall.
why: This happens on some VPNs, phone hotspots and broadband lines.
fix_summary: Use smaller pieces of data on this connection. The connection restarts for a moment.
undo: Run the fix again with the value 0 to go back to automatic.
manual: Set the MTU of the connection to 1400 in the network settings.

title: The newer internet address type (IPv6) is not working
what: The connection offers IPv6, but it does not work, so some sites hang before trying the older type.
why: A half-working IPv6 makes web pages slow to start.
fix_summary: Turn off IPv6 on the current connection. The normal internet keeps working.
undo: Run: nmcli connection modify NAME ipv6.method auto
manual: Turn IPv6 off in the connection's settings.

title: The VPN's safety switch is blocking all internet
what: The VPN is not connected, but its kill switch is still on, so nothing can reach the internet.
why: The kill switch cuts the internet on purpose when a VPN drops, so your traffic is never exposed.
fix_summary: Turn the VPN off, including its kill switch, so you are online again. You can turn it back on in the VPN settings.

title: Bluetooth is installed but not running
what: The Bluetooth service is stopped, so headphones, mice and keyboards cannot connect.
why: The service stops if it crashed or was switched off.

title: A Bluetooth adapter is there but has no driver
why: The adapter cannot be used until its driver or firmware is installed.
fix_summary: Install the missing drivers. Needs the internet.
undo: Remove the package with your package manager if needed.
manual: Connect a cable and run: sudo secure-linux-drivers install

title: A network socket (Ethernet) has no driver
why: The cable socket cannot be used until its driver is installed.
fix_summary: Install the missing drivers. Use Wi-Fi or phone tethering for the internet.
undo: Remove the package with your package manager if needed.
